message.title: Lerøy Seafood Group ASA: Third quarter 2026 results
message.body:
LERØY SEAFOOD GROUP ASA: STRONG EARNINGS IMPROVEMENT, GOOD BIOLOGICAL
DEVELOPMENT AND STRONG CASH FLOW

"Operational EBIT in the third quarter of 2026 was NOK 459 million, compared
with NOK 15 million in the same quarter last year. The improvement reflects good
biological development and lower costs in Farming, as well as a strong quarter
in Market Operations. At the same time, we are delivering strong cash flow, and
net interest-bearing debt was reduced by NOK 676 million during the quarter,"
says CEO Henning Beltestad.

FARMING: GOOD BIOLOGICAL DEVELOPMENT AND LOWER COSTS

Operational EBIT in Farming was NOK 113 million in the third quarter of 2026,
compared with NOK -306 million in the same period last year. Harvest volume of
salmon and trout was 54,680 GWT, eight percent lower than the year before.

"We continue to see good biological development, and all three of our Norwegian
farming regions delivered improved results compared with the same quarter last
year. Cost levels have declined, while we have also built high standing biomass,
providing a good basis for the coming quarters," says Henning Beltestad.

Harvest volume guidance for Norway is maintained at 195,000 GWT for 2026, with
the same volume expected in 2027. Including the Group's share of Scottish Sea
Farms, total harvest volume is expected to be approximately 215,000 GWT in 2026
and approximately 217,500 GWT in 2027.

MARKET OPERATIONS: STRONG QUARTER

Market Operations delivered Operational EBIT of NOK 446 million in the third
quarter of 2026, compared with NOK 410 million in the same period last year. The
EBIT margin was 5.4 percent, up from 4.9 percent in the third quarter of 2025.
The improvement was mainly driven by higher earnings in primary processing.

"Market Operations delivered a strong quarter. This development is in line with
our previously communicated expectation of significantly improved earnings in
the second half of the year," says Henning Beltestad.

WILD CATCH: LOWER EXPECTATIONS FOR 2026

Operational EBIT in Wild Catch was NOK -20 million in the third quarter of
2026, compared with NOK 3 million in the same period last year. Catch volume
declined by 24 percent to 10,216 tonnes. Higher prices did not fully offset
lower catch volume and higher bunker fuel prices.

"Prices for saithe, cod and haddock have been weaker than previously assumed,
while bunker fuel costs have increased. Against this background, we are reducing
our expectation for Operational EBIT in Wild Catch in 2026 to NOK 315-350
million, compared with the previous expectation of NOK 400-450 million," says
Henning Beltestad.

STRONG CASH FLOW AND PROGRESS IN THE COST PROGRAMME

Cash flow from operating activities was NOK 1,183 million in the third quarter
of 2026, compared with NOK 1,078 million in the same period last year. Net
interest-bearing debt was reduced by NOK 676 million during the quarter to NOK
7,732 million. The equity ratio was 46.4 percent at the end of the quarter.

At the end of the third quarter, NOK 701 million of the Group's NOK 1 billion
cost programme had been realised, while measures representing a further NOK 262
million had been identified and were under implementation.

OUTLOOK

Lerøy enters the fourth quarter with high standing biomass and continued good
biological development. Following several quarters of strong growth, the global
supply of salmon and trout is expected to increase at a slower pace, while
demand remains strong. This points to a more favourable price environment.

The cost programme is progressing according to plan and is expected to reduce
the impact of higher feed prices in 2027.

"We enter the fourth quarter with good biological status, high standing biomass,
a lower cost level and a stronger financial position. At the same time, we
continue to see strong demand for salmon and lower global supply growth.
Together with further effects from the cost programme, this provides a solid
foundation for further development," concludes Henning Beltestad.
